summary_en: This study compares two radiation schedules for early-stage lung cancer that is in the outer (peripheral) parts of the lungs. Patients are randomly assigned to either 3 fractions given over 3 days, for a total of 54 Grays, or 5 fractions given over 5 days, for a total of 60 Grays, followed by follow-up with their radiation oncologist. The study looks at the kinds of side effects (toxicity) patients have with each schedule, and its official title describes it as a randomized phase II study.
summary_es: Este estudio compara dos esquemas de radiación para el cáncer de pulmón en etapa temprana que se encuentra en las partes externas (periféricas) de los pulmones. Los pacientes son asignados al azar a 3 fracciones administradas en 3 días, para una dosis total de 54 Grays, o a 5 fracciones administradas en 5 días, para una dosis total de 60 Grays, seguidos de un control con su oncólogo radioterapeuta. El estudio analiza qué tipos de efectos secundarios (toxicidad) presentan los pacientes con cada esquema, y su título oficial lo describe como un estudio aleatorizado de fase II.
who_for: Lung cancer of a non-small cell type, such as squamous, adenocarcinoma, or large cell
Stage I or II disease with T1 N0 M0, or T2 up to 5 cm with N0 M0
Zubrod performance status 0 to 2 within 4 weeks of study entry
Women who could become pregnant and men must use effective contraception
not_for: Central tumors located near the main airways (within 2 cm of the proximal bronchial tree)
Evidence of regional or distant spread after staging
Prior malignancy in the past 2 years, with some exceptions
Previous lung or mediastinal radiation, or planned concomitant antineoplastic therapy
